MACHINE

2.1 The central bolt and bottom flange support shall be in one piece and made of steel alloy conforming to fS : 4368-1967 ` Specification for alloy steel billets, blooms and slabs for forgings for general engineering purposes ' and heat treated to give a hardness of 300 to 340 HV. The hardness shall be measured on the 22 mm diameter section of the bolt. The preferred diameter of the central portion of the loading bolt is 19 mm, butthe dimension can be adjusted in order to ensure that the required relationship exists between stress and bolt extension. 2.2 The top~and bottom distance pieces, top nut, top and bottom flanges, holder for dial gauge and ~for steel for hardening clamps shall be made of steel conforming to IS :5517-1969 ` Specification and tempering `. The measuring bars (solid or floating type) and the pin for thermocouple shall be made of bright bars conforming to IS : 7270-1974 ' Specification for bright bars (standard quality) `. 2.3 The thermocouple junction is to be firmly pressed against the end of the thermocouple hole. .

\

2.4 The top and bottom flanges should be enclosed all round by a 1 kW heating element, suitably controlled to give a uniform temperature rise from room temperature to 300�C in one hour and to hold the.temperature within f5"C of this uniform rate at any time, as well as maintain the test temperature within f5"C for the test period. 2.5 The elasticity of the machine shall be such that the bolt extension (as given by the dial gauge, at the top of the apparatus ) required to produce an initial stress of 40 MPa on the gasket, shall not be less than 230 Km and not more than 300 pm. 2.6 The thermal characteristics off the apparatus are to be such that when a steel ring of the same size as the test piece, is used instead of the test piece, the maximum stress is within the limits of 43 to 47 MPa*. 2.7 The apparatus is to be insulated so that the rate of heating or the final temperature is held within the limits specified above and totally unaffected by any change in ambient temperature. before use and dia3. Calibration of Apparatus - It is essential that the apparatus is calibrated gram prepared so that the load applied to the test piece shall be read at different temperaturesas a function of the extension of the central bolt. The calibration method shall ensure that the central bolt is loaded in the same manner as occurs when the tests are conducted. 3.1 The method 3.2 A typical of calibration of the stress relaxation test apparatus is given in Appendix A.

calibration

diagram

is given in Fig. 3.

Preparation of Test Piece - The test piece shall be cut from 1'5 mm thick jointing,sheets. case of orders for jointing sheets of other thicknesses, the test piece shall.be cut from 1'5 mm thick jointing sheet guaranteed by the manu#cturer to be of equivalent-quality. It 4.1 Test piece shall be an annular ring of 75 mm external diameter and 55 mm internal diameter. should be cut with a die to ensure that there are no burrs on the edges and that the bore and outside diameter are concentric.

5. Procedure - The test piece shall be conditioned in a desiccator containing chloride for 48 hours at room temperature immediately prior to the test.

anhydrous

calcium

5.1 Rub french chalk or graphite on both. sides of the test piece to prevent the test piece from sticking to the top or bottom flanges. If preferred, thin aluminium foil may be placed between the flanges and the test pierce. 5.2 Assemble the apparatus with the test piece placed concentrically between the flanges.

5.3 Set the dial gauge to zero. 5.4 Stress the test piece by tightening the nut, without jerking to the initial compressive strength of 40 MPa, that is, by tightening the nut until the dial gauge reading reaches the figure corresponding to 40 MPa on the room temperature curve of the calibration diagram. -5.5 The nut shall be re-tightened after five minutes compensate for any relaxation that has occurred. .5.6 Switch the heat on and raise the temperature as mentioned in 2.4. to the initial compressive stress as in 5.4 to

EXPLANATORY
This standard, first published compr,essed asbestos fibre jointing Gaskets must have the initial tightening of time and at the required to the gasket is referred in 1971, has been revised materials.

NOTE
to make it suitable for high temperature

the ability to maintain the stress level applied to the flanged assembly in the interfaces if an adequate seal is to be maintained for a long period of Any reduction in this stress level directly attributable service te,mperature. to as gasket stress relaxation or simply as relaxation. in this standard is therefore the given stress as function intended to assess the quality of temperature and time, of materials

The method described and their ability to maintain

The relaxation stress of the material is the value obtained on the calibration diagram corresponding to the difference between dial gauge readings at the end of the test and after releasing the tension in the bolt. With the introduction of this test, other tests may not be necessary to asse,ss the suitability _ the material for temperature and pressure parameters. Therefore, the results obtained should correlated with actual working conditions. While preparing this standard, assistance has been derived from BS 2815 : 1973 `Compressed asbestos fibre jointing', issued by the-British Standards Institution. 9
